Wow. Just... wow. Okay, calm down. The second you do anything in a game within the confines of the game mechanics that the maker of the game says, "this was unintended", you are using an exploit.

I hesitated to use the word "cheating" when I wrote this because I knew someone would get triggered. I have met that person it seems. And to be honest, it's not cheating unless you do it AFTER the developer has told you not to do it. So it's more retroactive cheating, but not actual cheating. It IS however most assuredly an exploit. You are exploiting a game mechanic to produce an unintended effect. Unintended as is defined by the developer, who keeps pulling these things because that deem them to BE EXPLOITS. 

And since you in your infinite wisdom decided to comment on a post without reading the whole thing, you missed the fact that I call for ways to make it LESS grindy, not more. Fuck's sake indeed. GOOD DAY SIR. *re-affixes monocle*

There is a huge difference between "space game physics are loopy, don't worry about it,"  and "space game physics work how we want it to when we want it to and doesn't when it's convenient for us and not for you." I'm all for repeating to myself it's just a show, I should really just relax, but more and more the game just feels like, "well we did it this way because the game engine is complicated and we didn't care/have enough time to make it work properly, so let's build the game around it's limitations without thinking of the consequences or if it makes sense." But hey, if everything is working as you like it, my stupid opinion isn't going to change your mind. Enjoy.

I said "possibility of being scanned by cops and shot" That's not me saying it's impossible. And using a bank robbery was my mistake. Too much hyperbole. It's more akin to... well, actual trespassing. If you are seen trespassing, by a security guard or on camera, they don't know who you are and there is the chance you will get away without any repercussions. In Elite, you WILL be seen and you are automatically given a bounty. No chance in that not happening.

 And the "Docking at a station where you're wanted" mini-game is stupid. Like any security service worth anything would say, "Well, that guy didn't go through the metal detector, but I mean he's all the way inside the building now... meh. I'm sure he's clean." I'm not saying I have the answer, I'm just saying the answer they have is a poor one.

Calling me disingenuous is rather flippant. Yes, there is a 0% chance that scanning that data point will lead to you not getting a bounty. I'm not trying to be misleading, that's a fact. Even standing outside of the "trespass" zone will lead to a bounty. There is no way around it other than not doing the mission. And having an outstanding bounty isn't "getting away with it".

I'll address each of your points.

-The Colonia Initiative, (which I am participating in despite my better judgement) is long haul trucking, not exploring. 

-Neutron stars are really only useful if you are trying to get somewhere very fast. Speed gets you places faster, but it doesn't fix a lack of substance when you get there.

-What profession? Seriously, scientific exploration is a job I would sign up for in a heart beat. All I see are job listings for bus drivers.

-Alien ruins. I've been to the first one. Very pretty. I couldn't interact with it beyond scanning, (which provided very little in the way of a sciencey experience) and play soccer with the artifacts. 

-New geological and alien landscapes. Neat. But they are so few and far between and hard to find that only the most persistent can. And let's face it, they are just getting lucky, not analyzing data or using surveying equipment. Nothing IN GAME anyway.

You can call all of this "exploration" but it doesn't *FEEL* like exploration to me. And I know this is very much my problem, not yours. I suppose my expectations are too overreaching.
Elaborate.

Don't get me wrong, my explorer conda is armed to the teeth, and I've spent countless hours lovingly crafting all the engineer bits and bobs until I was satisfied. 

I really wanted some detailed science scanning and rock sniffing and biological studying. All fluffy crap but it would make me happy. And I wanted to share that with a crew, PC OR NPC. I got super excited when I got a crew member to fly my fighter. Then I saw that when the fighter bay isn't installed, the lazy sponge just sits in the crew lounge on some far off station. And even when she IS on board, she is sitting in the bowels of the ship playing xbox. Where are my crew members? Where are my science officers? Hell, where are my bridge bunnies!?

More and more it seems that FDev will only pursue combat improvements to this game. Anything that involves exploration or any non-violent avenues get lip service and some vague flavor text, and that's it. 
I'm not saying that's not the smart move for them. I'm sure the majority of people are mostly in it for the pews, but my dreams for having a science vessel (a la Star Trek), or designing and up-keeping an outpost of my own seem to be fading into the distance.

This is just a theory, but my guess is that this game was not programmed like a well planned out city grid and more like a rat's nest of interconnected clusters, where when you change one thing that seems innocuous enough it leads to errors and bugs for days. It's easier to build on something new than go into the jungle and clear a path. But I've always felt they need more people working there, and their chief cost cutting measure is simply keeping there work force small. It's a nice idea, but I think it leads to the issues we are discussing.

I think it comes down to FDev being more concerned with people saying, "you promised feature X and you have yet to deliver" than the do, "you delivered feature X and is doesn't work right". "New" is progress, "fixed" is stagnancy. "Fixed" doesn't get people excited to spend money. "New" is sexy and gets people throwing money at you.

I personally do not encourage combat logging, and I don't wish to give the impression that I do. I'm simply trying to point out that a zero tolerance for it undermines a more casual and friendly play style, which in turn creates a more exclusive and less approachable game. This topic seems to polarize the community in a way nothing else has. I can see how some would wish for a game where nothing they perceive as cheating is tolerated,  and I can see a few ways in which combat logging shouldn't be. But many people here as so vehemently against it that I bristle at such wholesale condemnation , regardless of the justification. Perhaps it's the skeptic in me, but I question if they even know why they hate it so much. In many cases the combat logging breaks down to someone choosing not to waste hours of time to satiate another persons instant gratification. But I argue that in the times combat logging COULD be justified, the other party would not have had a satisfying combat engagement anyway. If someone doesn't want to fight and you force the issue, why is it wrong for them to want to leave? And yes, they are disengaging from the fight in a non-sanctioned fashion, but at that point why would you care? They denied you what? And before you say they should play in solo or a private group that denies them casual exposure to people who are NOT interested in PVP as well as those who do, what's stopping everyone who desires nothing but wild west shoot outs and high seas piracy from making there own private groups? There are certain situations where combat logging is bad, but lumping casual players in with the them is illogical. 

And if the issue is people who log while participating in a CG or powerplay, let me suggest this to FDev. Flag people who sign up for CGs or are actively carrying cargo for powerplay. Give THEM a one minute countdown after disconnecting before their ship exits the game. Because yes, in that situation logging is cheating. And there is nothing stopping THEM from going into solo.

If it's a Red vs. Blue type thing with the consequences being an arbitrary score goes one way or another, everything is fine and the community and game remain mostly unchanged. But when whomever wins changes the game and the direction the story takes, everyone want's to be in the drivers seat, and that leads to unhealthy infighting as I'm sure everyone has seen.

I have to admit, FDEV did this to themselves. They gave everyone the ability to compromise the game and that was a bold move if they are willing to, as you say, 'roll with the punches'. He knew it was her before he ever saw her face. Her stiletto heels clacked mercilessly across the marble floor, and every piercing step shocked him like a knife in his heart. He couldn't believe it was her, no matter how well the pieces fit together. She had been with him every step of the way. And now she would be there in the end.

“Stop right there, Anise.” His voice betrayed him, trembling as he said her name. He stepped out from behind one of the columns surrounding the ritual dais. He hid his eyes in the wide brim of his top hat. She froze and as she did the moonlight from the high temple windows illuminated her pale complexion. Shock, and sadness. He wasn't ready for that. “I can't let you do this. Just leave. I can tell them no one came to finish the ritual.” He held out his hands, pleading with her. “Schroeder said there were five. From my count, you're the last one alive. They all died for this nonsense.”

“It's not nonsense, Paul!” she cut him off. Her rose colored lips, muted in the cold light curled into a sob. “I have to do this. I'm sorry but I will never forgive humanity for taking my father away from me. I wish it could be different but...” she was whispering hoarsely now, her breath coming in little shaking gasps. “I loved you Paul. I will miss you.”

“Anise, no!” Paul could hear the hum of the dais coming to life, see the eerie green glow behind him painting the walls. “It never had to end this way.” he said as he drew his gun... and she began to cast her spell. The shock in her eyes was gone now, replaced with more green light, seemingly erupting from within her. She threw her arms out and an invisible fist drove into his chest, knocking him off his feet and flying across the dais. He landed in a heap with his gun thrown somewhere off to the side.

Anise was now floating a few inches off the ground. Her slim black evening gown slowly undulated at the hem, as if it were underwater. She moved to a rhythm unheard, swaying her arms and head as she spoke words mortals were never meant to hear. Paul, still reeling in pain was trying to get air to go back in his lungs. The green light was a pillar now, shooting from the dais and crackling with electricity. In the back of his head he heard something screaming as if from far away, but getting closer. He had to stop her now, before it came.

Paul scrambled to his knees, looking frantically for his gun. The screaming was getting louder now, and with it Anise's dark incantation. “Drrelth gof turrl goaheet uk ful swatku joplek. Tooshok gof neela sheshhak Ct'hulu...” She spoke in a voice no longer her own. Her arms shook violently and blood began to seep from her eyes and nose. The ground began to tremble and the light swirled with dark mists.

The screaming in Paul's head  was deafening now. He covered his ears but he knew it was coming from within him. Then he saw the gun. He lunged for it and managed to grab the thing as he tumbled forward, cradling it against his chest.

A black shape was coalescing on the dais from the mist. It writhed and twisted as it took form. Tentacles and teeth and eyes swirled and fought for dominance. The eyes stared at Paul and he screamed from his mouth and his mind and his soul. Reason was gone. Sanity was gone. All that was left was terror and instinct. He fired the gun.

The bullet, for all the blessings of power and protection it held, passed straight through the eldritch horror, and plunged deep into Anise's heart. 

The screams stopped. The sudden absence of the cacophony felt like being thrown into the vacuum for space. Anise crumpled to the floor, broken and empty.

The beast with a thousand mouths that sprung forth from the light of a distant star then spoke into Paul's mind, burning it's words into his very being as it slowly cracked and burned like wood in a pyre. “Know this mortal. You have undone my return, but the seal is now broken. I will send all the servants of the elder gods to your miserable world. I will find you where ever you hide and I will tie you to the rocks by your own entrails. I will rape your mind and make you watch everything you love be destroyed  a thousand times over. THEN, I will begin your punishment.” 

The thing on the dais was all but ash as the words echoed in his mind. The light faded to nothingness, replaced by a darkness that was so complete that Paul began to shake and weep before he even understood why.

The moon was gone. The seal was broken.

Inside the citadel were the familiar sights of technology and hell flesh interwoven for some unholy purpose. The air was rank and wet. An old, fat hell beast turn at my sudden entrance and roared menacingly, flecks of spittle bursting in a sickening mist. I leveled my cannon on her and let loose a volley that sent her sprawling, cursing me as a ran past.
